Use the repository's written documentation as review context and check whether the change matches the documented intent.

- Start from README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and docs/ADRs/ for architectural context.
- This library is intentionally minimal and shared. Check that changes do not introduce Delivery SDK or Management SDK domain logic. See ARCHITECTURE.md § Overview.
- Check whether code, tests, and documentation all tell the same story. Flag mismatches between implementation and the documented architecture or ADRs.
- Treat AGENTS.md as the authoritative guide for sharp edges and invariants. If a change violates an invariant documented there, flag it.
- If CI or another required check already enforces a merge rule (e.g., the backwards-compatibility check), do not ask for duplicate PR template sections or manual checklists.
- Ask for an ADR update when a change is architecture-significant: new external dependency, new integration, change to the HTTP pipeline, change to the exception dispatch model, or change to the User-Agent header format.
- Distinguish public API from internal implementation. All classes in src/ are potentially public surface — changes to constructor signatures, method signatures, or return types require extra scrutiny.
- If a change drops support for a PHP version or Composer package constraint without a major version bump, flag it as a BC break.
